title: Scalar extension respects ordinary etale derived direct-image exchange
statement:
Let $\varphi:A\to B$ be a unital map of finite commutative rings. All schemes and morphisms below are arbitrary [def-pc-scheme]. Write $D_R(T)=D(T_{\mathrm{et}},R)$ for the ordinary unbounded derived category of constant-ring module sheaves [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], $Q_T=(-)\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], and $u_R^*$ for exact inverse image [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]. Use the canonical K-flat scalar/pullback isomorphism $\lambda_u:u_B^*Q_T\cong Q_Wu_A^*$ for $u:W\to T$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Use the canonical derived adjunction $u_R^*\dashv Ru_{*,R}$ [def-kun-projection-formula-map]. Define $\chi_{u,E}:Q_TRu_{*,A}E\to Ru_{*,B}Q_WE$ to have adjunct $Q_W(\varepsilon_{u,A,E})\circ\lambda_{u,Ru_{*,A}E}$, where $\varepsilon_{u,A}$ is the counit. Let $X'\xrightarrow hX$, $f':X'\to Y'$, $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y'\to Y$ form a cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square]. For $R=A,B$, let $\operatorname{Ex}_R:g_R^*Rf_{*,R}\to Rf'_{*,R}h_R^*$ be the specified unbounded counit exchange [def-kun-unbounded-exchange]. For every $M\in D_A(X)$,
$$Rf'_{*,B}(\lambda_{h,M})\circ\operatorname{Ex}_{B,Q_XM}\circ g_B^*(\chi_{f,M})=\chi_{f',h_A^*M}\circ Q_{Y'}(\operatorname{Ex}_{A,M})\circ\lambda_{g,Rf_{*,A}M}.$$
This is an equality from $g_B^*Q_YRf_{*,A}M$ to $Rf'_{*,B}Q_{X'}h_A^*M$, natural in $M$. Neither properness nor an isomorphism conclusion for either exchange or scalar mate is assumed.

source.place: Tag 0E47, label remark-compose-base-change-horizontal; counit verification for the coefficient and geometric square

proof.text: Apply the existing small-etale normalized composition law [lem-sf-scalar-pullback-composition] to the two paths h followed by f and f' followed by g, with common composite h ≫ f = f' ≫ g. These laws already use scalarPullbackIso transported to exact inverse image, namely properOpenCoefficientPullbackIso, so no general ringed-module inverse-image construction or tensor switch is required. Write c_h,R and c_g,R for their exact derived composition comparisons. By definition [def-kun-unbounded-exchange], the specified square comparison is c_g,R inverse followed by c_h,R: expand squareUpperStarIso and mapDerivedCategoryNatIso on composition and inverses. Precompose the desired cube with c_g,B, cancel its inverse, use the two composition laws, and cancel c_g,A after scalar extension. This gives, for every N, theta_B(QN) followed by h_B*(lambda_f,N) followed by lambda_h,f_A*N equals f'_B*(lambda_g,N) followed by lambda_f',g_A*N followed by Q(theta_A,N), exactly with the square comparison defining the exchange.

source.place: Tag 0E47, remark-compose-base-change-horizontal, with Tag 07A7, remark-base-change; explicit counit verification omitted by the source

proof.text:
The derived adjunctions used below are the canonical ones of [def-kun-projection-formula-map]. The mate formula of [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], applied to the definition of $\chi$ in the statement, gives
$$\varepsilon_{u,B,Q_WE}\circ P_{u,B}(\chi_{u,E})=Q_W(\varepsilon_{u,A,E})\circ\lambda_{u,F_{u,A}E}.\tag{C}$$
The definition of the specified exchange [def-kun-unbounded-exchange] gives, for $R=A,B$,
$$\varepsilon_{f',R,P_{h,R}E}\circ P_{f',R}(\operatorname{Ex}_{R,E})
=P_{h,R}(\varepsilon_{f,R,E})\circ\theta_{R,F_{f,R}E}.\tag{E}$$
These equations are just the two defining adjoint-transpose equations; they do not assert invertibility of either map.

source.place: Tag 0E47, remark-compose-base-change-horizontal, with Tag 07A7, remark-base-change; explicit counit verification omitted by the source

proof.text:
Fix $M\in D_A(X)$ and put $N=F_{f,A}M$. Transpose the left side of the desired identity under $P_{f',B}\dashv F_{f',B}$: apply $P_{f',B}$ and then its counit. Counit naturality at $\lambda_{h,M}$ and (E) identify this transpose with
$$\lambda_{h,M}\circ P_{h,B}(\varepsilon_{f,B,Q_XM})\circ\theta_{B,F_{f,B}Q_XM}\circ P_{f',B}P_{g,B}(\chi_{f,M}).$$
Naturality of $\theta_B$ at $\chi_{f,M}$ moves the last map past $\theta_B$, giving $P_{h,B}P_{f,B}(\chi_{f,M})\circ\theta_{B,Q_YN}$. Substitute (C) for $u=f,E=M$, and then use naturality of $\lambda_h$ at $\varepsilon_{f,A,M}:P_{f,A}N\to M$. The resulting transpose is
$$T_L=Q_{X'}P_{h,A}(\varepsilon_{f,A,M})\circ\lambda_{h,P_{f,A}N}\circ P_{h,B}(\lambda_{f,N})\circ\theta_{B,Q_YN}.$$
Every rewrite is naturality or one of the explicit transpose equations in Step 2 [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate, def-kun-unbounded-exchange].

source.place: Tag 0E47, remark-compose-base-change-horizontal, with Tag 07A7, remark-base-change; explicit counit verification omitted by the source

proof.text:
Transpose the right side under the same adjunction. Equation (C) for $u=f',E=P_{h,A}M$ first gives
$$Q_{X'}(\varepsilon_{f',A,P_{h,A}M})\circ\lambda_{f',F_{f',A}P_{h,A}M}\circ P_{f',B}(Q_{Y'}(\operatorname{Ex}_{A,M}))\circ P_{f',B}(\lambda_{g,N}).$$
Naturality of $\lambda_{f'}$ at $\operatorname{Ex}_{A,M}$ replaces its middle pair by $Q_{X'}P_{f',A}(\operatorname{Ex}_{A,M})\circ\lambda_{f',P_{g,A}N}$. Combine the first two factors by functoriality of $Q_{X'}$ and apply (E) for $R=A,E=M$. Thus the transpose is
$$T_R=Q_{X'}P_{h,A}(\varepsilon_{f,A,M})\circ Q_{X'}(\theta_{A,N})\circ\lambda_{f',P_{g,A}N}\circ P_{f',B}(\lambda_{g,N}).$$
As in Step 3 these are precisely the transpose formula and naturality, with no resolution or acyclicity assertion [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate, def-kun-unbounded-exchange].

source.place: Tag 0E47, remark-compose-base-change-horizontal, with Tag 07A7, remark-base-change; explicit counit verification omitted by the source

proof.text: Postcompose equation (*) of Step 1 with $Q_{X'}P_{h,A}(\varepsilon_{f,A,M})$ to obtain $T_L=T_R$. The Hom bijection of the canonical derived adjunction [def-kun-projection-formula-map], with its counit transpose formula [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], is injective, so the original two morphisms are equal. Their common source and target are those in the statement, since $N=F_{f,A}M$. Naturality in $M$ follows because $\lambda$, $\theta$, the counits and their mates are natural transformations and composition and whiskering preserve their naturality. This proves the identity for every unbounded $M$ and every square in the statement.
